Package src/ticket_triage/ containing:
- errors.py: ServiceError (always the fixed message "Model service unavailable.", constructed with no underlying text, never carrying the key or the cause) and InvalidModelOutput (attribute raw_reply holding the exact reply string).
- guard.py: refuse when text.strip() == "" or len(text) > 4000 (len counts Unicode code points; the text is never trimmed before measuring).
- contract.py: pure functions only. parse_reply(raw) parses with json.loads using an object_pairs_hook that rejects duplicate keys at every depth and a parse_constant hook that rejects NaN and Infinity; any failure, a non-object, an unexpected key set, a wrong type or enum value, or any violated invariant raises InvalidModelOutput(raw) with the exact raw string. Never repair or normalise. Invariant checks: exactly six keys; action-to-field consistency; summary 1-200 and clarification_question 5-200 ending in "?" (len on str); refusal_reason invalid_input rejected; after removing spaces and hyphens from every string field no run of 13 or more ASCII digits ([0-9]{13,}); no match of sk-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,} and no literal OPENAI_API_KEY.
- model_client.py: ModelClient protocol with one method complete(system: str, user: str) -> str.
- openai_client.py: OpenAIClient implementing ModelClient. It reads OPENAI_API_KEY and OPENAI_MODEL from os.environ inside complete(), at call time, and raises ServiceError before any network activity if either is missing or empty after stripping. It calls openai.OpenAI(api_key=..., timeout=30.0, max_retries=0) so the evaluation harness controls retries, then chat.completions.create with model, a system message, a user message, and response_format={"type": "json_object"}. Do not pass temperature and do not use strict structured outputs, so schema violations stay visible to the independent harness. If the reply content is None, return an empty string. Catch openai.OpenAIError only and raise ServiceError from None. Never log, print or include the key or the underlying error text anywhere.
- prompts.py: loads the system prompt text from prompts/system.md (path resolved from the package location to the Part-1B prompts folder).
- service.py: triage(ticket_text, client=None) -> dict. It applies the guard first and returns the six-key refusal decision for invalid_input without creating a client, reading any environment variable, or calling the model. Otherwise it uses the supplied client or, if None, OpenAIClient(); sends the system prompt and the ticket text as the user message (exactly the ticket text, nothing added); validates the reply with contract.parse_reply; and returns the decision dict.
- cli.py: main(argv, client=None) -> int. It checks len(argv) only (no option parser), reads the file as bytes, decodes strict UTF-8, removes one leading U+FEFF if present, calls triage, and returns 0, 2, 3 or 4 with exactly the specified stdout and stderr text. Output is bytes written to sys.stdout.buffer or sys.stderr.buffer: json.dumps(decision, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False) encoded as UTF-8 plus b"\n". Never use print. Catch only ServiceError and InvalidModelOutput at the top level; the raw reply is never printed.
- env_loader.py and __main__.py: __main__ may load KEY=VALUE lines from an untracked .env file in the Part-1B folder into os.environ only for names that are not already set, using a small parser in env_loader.py, then call cli.main. The library modules never read .env.

The system prompt is identical for every ticket.

 # Support Ticket Triage Assistant Constitution
 
 ## Core Principles
 
 ### I. Modular Boundaries and Secret Isolation
 The library MUST separate deterministic input guarding, prompt construction, the model-client
 interface, response parsing and validation, and the thin command-line layer. Prompt text MUST
 reside in files under `prompts/`, never in source code. All network access and application reading
 of the API key MUST be confined to one small OpenAI client module behind the model-client
 interface, so tests can inject a fake client. The key MUST come from `OPENAI_API_KEY` and the
 model name from `OPENAI_MODEL`. The command-line layer and harness MAY load these values from an
 untracked `.env` file. The values MUST NOT appear in source, logs, error messages, or output.
 
 ### II. Untrusted Input and Deterministic Guardrails
 Ticket text MUST be treated as untrusted data: it MUST never be executed or used as a file path,
 command, or tool argument, and MUST NOT change application instructions or the output schema.
 The deterministic input guard MUST reject empty, whitespace-only, and oversized input before any
 model call; each such refusal MUST make zero model calls.
 
 ### III. Validated Triage Contract and Explicit Failures
 The output MUST conform to the output schema contract defined in the specification. Responses
 MUST be parsed and validated against that contract before they are returned as triage decisions.
 Network, timeout, rate-limit, authentication, and other model or service failures MUST raise a
 distinct error type and MUST never be represented as a triage result.
 
 ### IV. Independent Evaluation and Acceptance
 An independent evaluation harness MUST decide acceptance. Acceptance requires 100 percent schema
 validity, 100 percent structural-invariant compliance, 100 percent pass on guardrail cases, and
 an aggregate score at or above the threshold and scoring formula stated in the specification
 before evaluation begins. A language-model judge MAY contribute to aggregate scoring, but MUST
 NOT replace schema validation or invariant checks.
 
 ### V. Minimal Dependencies and Maintainability
 The runtime MUST use Python 3.12 or later and the official `openai` package as its only
 third-party runtime dependency. Solutions MUST prefer simple, maintainable implementations over
 unnecessary complexity.
 
 ## Technical Constraints
 
 Development tools MAY include `pytest`, `pytest-cov`, `ruff`, `bandit`, and `jsonschema`. The
 harness MAY populate `OPENAI_API_KEY` and `OPENAI_MODEL` from an untracked `.env` file; `.env`
 files MUST NOT be committed. API keys and credentials MUST NOT be committed or written to
 evidence or logs.
 
 ## Evaluation and Scope Controls
 
 Before any evaluation, the specification MUST define the output schema contract, structural
 invariants, behavioral properties, guardrail rules, evaluation threshold, and scoring formula.
 Every acceptance criterion and invariant in the specification MUST map to at least one test or
 evaluation case.
 
 The independent harness MUST enforce all of the following deterministic-code quality standards:
 
 - `ruff` reports zero errors.
 - `bandit` reports zero medium- or high-severity findings.
 - All deterministic tests pass.
 - Line coverage of `src/` is at least 90 percent, excluding only the thin OpenAI client module,
   which is exercised by the live evaluation.
 
 The `tests/`, `evals/`, and `.harness/` directories are owned by the human engineer and are
 outside the scope of Spec Kit implementation tasks. Generated task lists MUST NOT include tasks
 to create or modify those directories, though tasks MAY reference them for traceability. During
 implementation and repair, the coding agent MAY change only `src/` and `prompts/`. It MUST NOT
 modify the specification, `tests/`, `evals/`, or `.harness/`; delete or weaken tests, assertions,
 or evaluation cases; change expected results; lower thresholds; disable guardrails, lint, or
 security checks; bypass harness gates; or manually edit recorded results. Marking completed tasks 
 in `tasks.md` during implementation is permitted.
 
 ## Governance
 
 Constitution amendments MUST be made through the Spec Kit constitution workflow, with the
 rationale recorded and the version and amendment date updated. Changes to specification
 artifacts MUST be made only through the applicable Spec Kit commands (`specify`, `clarify`,
 `plan`, or `tasks`), and each legitimate specification change MUST record its reason.
 
 Versioning MUST follow semantic versioning: MAJOR for backward-incompatible governance or
 principle removals or redefinitions, MINOR for new principles or sections or materially expanded
 guidance, and PATCH for clarifications and non-semantic refinements. Compliance MUST be reviewed
 against this constitution and the specification; the independent harness MUST enforce the
 specified acceptance and deterministic-code quality gates before acceptance.
 
 **Version**: 1.0.0 | **Ratified**: 2026-11-01 | **Last Amended**: 2026-11-01

 # Feature Specification: Support Ticket Triage Assistant
 
 **Feature Branch**: Not specified
 
 **Created**: 2026-11-01
 
 **Status**: Approved
 
 **Input**: Build a library function and command-line tool that turn one customer support ticket into a structured triage decision with language-model assistance.
 
 ## Clarifications
 
 ### Session 2026-11-01
 
 - Q: Which unit defines a “character” for non-BMP Unicode characters and combining-character sequences when applying the 4000-character input guard and output length limits? → A: Unicode code points; combining marks count separately, and each non-BMP code point counts once.
 - Q: Which exact character set counts as a “key character” after `sk-` in the API-key pattern? → A: ASCII letters, digits, underscores, and hyphens.
 - Q: Does “secrets” in GR-005 include sensitive values beyond the specified card-number and API-key patterns, and, if so, which detectable forms are in scope? → A: Only the listed patterns.
 - Q: Does “up to 3 attempts” mean three attempts total or an initial attempt followed by up to three retries? → A: Three attempts total: one initial attempt and up to two retries.
 - Q: When a ticket does not state whether a workaround exists, what evidence is sufficient to distinguish `medium` from `high` priority? → A: Dataset gold with one-level tolerance.
 - Q: How does evaluation handle an application-raised `InvalidModelOutput`? → A: The case is `FAIL` with score 0, not `ERROR`; evaluation independently runs Layers 1 and 2 on the exact raw reply carried by the exception and records every violation found.
 - Q: How often is each evaluation case run, and how are service errors retried? → A: Each case is evaluated exactly once per run; a service-error attempt may be retried up to two times, for three attempts total.
 - Q: What happens when model configuration is missing or empty? → A: If a model call is needed, missing or empty `OPENAI_API_KEY` or `OPENAI_MODEL` raises `ServiceError` with the fixed message and makes no model call; input-guard refusals require neither value.
 - Q: How does the command-line tool read and decode ticket files? → A: It reads bytes, decodes strict UTF-8 without newline translation, removes one leading UTF-8 byte-order mark before the input guard, and treats a missing path, directory, or invalid UTF-8 as `error: cannot read input file`.
 - Q: Which file-read failures must acceptance criterion AC-027 cover? → A: A missing path, a directory path, and a file containing the single byte `0xFF` each produce exit 2 with `error: cannot read input file`.
 - Q: What is the expected result for a ticket file with a leading UTF-8 byte-order mark? → A: With the specified billing ticket and reply `T`, it produces exactly the command-line output in AC-022.
 - Q: How does the command-line input guard count CR LF at the length boundary? → A: A file with 3999 `x` characters followed by CR LF has 4001 characters, receives the invalid-input decision with zero model calls, and exits 0.
 
 ## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*
 
 ### User Story 1 - Triage one support ticket (Priority: P1)
 
 A support worker submits one plain-text customer ticket and receives a structured decision that identifies its category and urgency, asks for the missing problem description when the request is too vague, or refuses text that is not a support request.
 
 **Why this priority**: This is the core user value: consistently routing a single support request without losing the distinction between an actionable ticket, a vague request, and unrelated or manipulative text.
 
 **Independent Test**: Submit one ticket at a time using a fake model with a specified reply. Verify the decision, model-call count, and any raised error without requiring the command-line tool.
 
 **Acceptance Scenarios**:
 
 1. **Given** a non-empty ticket of at most 4000 characters and a valid triage reply, **When** the library function processes it, **Then** it returns the same six decision values as the reply.
 2. **Given** a support request that does not say what the problem is, **When** it is processed, **Then** the decision asks one clarifying question.
 3. **Given** text that is not a support request, **When** it is processed, **Then** it is refused with `not_a_support_ticket`.
 4. **Given** text whose purpose is to control the assistant rather than describe a support problem, **When** it is processed, **Then** it is refused with `prompt_injection`.
 5. **Given** a genuine support problem that also contains instructions to control the assistant, **When** it is processed, **Then** the genuine problem is triaged and the embedded instructions do not change the result.
 6. **Given** a model reply that violates any contract invariant, **When** it is processed, **Then** an `InvalidModelOutput` error carries the exact raw reply and no repaired decision is returned.
 7. **Given** a model or service failure, **When** it is processed, **Then** a separate `ServiceError` is raised with the fixed, non-sensitive message.
 
 ### User Story 2 - Triage a ticket from a file (Priority: P2)
 
 A user gives the command-line tool one path to a UTF-8 text file. For a decision, the tool prints one compact JSON line and exits successfully; for an input or service error, it prints only the prescribed error line and exits with the prescribed status.
 
 **Why this priority**: The command-line tool provides a direct way to use the same dependable decision behavior with a saved ticket.
 
 **Independent Test**: Run the tool with temporary ticket files and controlled model replies or failures; assert standard output, standard error, and exit status separately.
 
 **Acceptance Scenarios**:
 
 1. **Given** exactly one readable ticket file and any valid triage, clarify, or refuse decision, **When** the tool runs, **Then** it prints that decision as compact JSON with alphabetically ordered keys and exits 0.
 2. **Given** an incorrect argument count, unreadable UTF-8 input, service failure, or invalid model reply, **When** the tool runs, **Then** it prints no decision to standard output and exits with the corresponding specified status and error line.
 
 ### User Story 3 - Evaluate behavior against defined cases (Priority: P3)
 
 A maintainer evaluates a fixed, traceable set of representative and adversarial tickets against known expected decisions, structural rules, privacy guardrails, and quality thresholds.
 
 **Why this priority**: A measurable evaluation makes correctness and safety requirements repeatable rather than dependent on informal review.
 
 **Independent Test**: Run the evaluation with controlled decisions and service errors, and verify per-case scores, statuses, and the overall result against the specified rules.

The `json_object` format is recognized, but the SDK describes it as an older JSON-generation method and says the system or user message must instruct the model to produce JSON. JSON mode produces valid JSON, not schema-constrained output, and requires a compatible model. ([Chat Completions example](https://github.com/openai/openai-python/blob/main/README.md#L47-L65), [request parameters](https://github.com/openai/openai-python/blob/main/src/openai/types/chat/completion_create_params.py#L42-L48), [JSON response format type](https://github.com/openai/openai-python/blob/main/src/openai/types/shared_params/response_format_json_object.py#L10-L19), [official JSON-mode guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/structured-outputs), [Chat Completions API reference](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/chat))

application. The library includes type definitions for all request params and response fields,

The REST API documentation can be found on [platform.openai.com](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference). The full API of this library can be found in [api.md](api.md).

## Installation

```sh

```

## Usage

The full API of this library can be found in [api.md](api.md).

The primary API for interacting with OpenAI models is the [Responses API](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/responses). You can generate text from the model with the code below.

```python
import os
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    # This is the default and can be omitted
    api_key=os.environ.get("OPENAI_API_KEY"),
)

response = client.responses.create(
    model="gpt-5.5",
    instructions="You are a coding assistant that talks like a pirate.",
    input="How do I check if a Python object is an instance of a class?",
)

print(response.output_text)
```

The previous standard (supported indefinitely) for generating text is the [Chat Completions API](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/chat). You can use that API to generate text from the model with the code below.

```python
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI()

completion = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="gpt-5.5",
    messages=[
        {"role": "developer", "content": "Talk like a pirate."},
        {
            "role": "user",
            "content": "How do I check if a Python object is an instance of a class?",
        },
    ],
)

print(completion.choices[0].message.content)
```

we recommend using [python-dotenv](https://pypi.org/project/python-dotenv/)
to add `OPENAI_API_KEY="My API Key"` to your `.env` file

[Get an API key here](https://platform.openai.com/settings/organization/api-keys).

```python
from openai import OpenAI

    workload_identity={
        "identity_provider_id": "idp-123",
        "service_account_id": "sa-456",
        "provider": k8s_service_account_token_provider("/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token"),
    },
)

    model="gpt-5.5",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}],
)
```

```python
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    workload_identity={
        "identity_provider_id": "idp-123",
        "service_account_id": "sa-456",
        "provider": azure_managed_identity_token_provider(
            resource="https://management.azure.com/",

    },
)
```

```python

client = OpenAI(
    workload_identity={
        "identity_provider_id": "idp-123",
        "service_account_id": "sa-456",
        "provider": gcp_id_token_provider(audience="https://api.openai.com/v1"),
    },
```

```python
        "refresh_buffer_seconds": 120.0,
```

text.format




Structured Outputs is available in two forms in the OpenAI API:

1. When using [function calling](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/function-calling)
2. When using a `json_schema` response format

Function calling is useful when you are building an application that bridges the models and functionality of your application.

For example, you can give the model access to functions that query a database in order to build an AI assistant that can help users with their orders, or functions that can interact with the UI.

Conversely, Structured Outputs via `response_format` are more suitable when you want to indicate a structured schema for use when the model responds to the user, rather than when the model calls a tool.

For example, if you are building a math tutoring application, you might want the assistant to respond to your user using a specific JSON Schema so that you can generate a UI that displays different parts of the model's output in distinct ways.

In practice:




  - If you are connecting the model to tools, functions, data, etc. in your
  system, then you should use function calling - If you want to structure the
  model's output when it responds to the user, then you should use a structured
  `text.format`





  The remainder of this guide will focus on non-function calling use cases in
    the Responses API. To learn more about how to use Structured Outputs with
    function calling, check out the 
    [Function Calling](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/function-calling#strict-mode) 
    guide.


### Structured Outputs vs JSON mode

Structured Outputs is the evolution of [JSON mode](#json-mode). While both ensure valid JSON is produced, only Structured Outputs ensure schema adherence. Both Structured Outputs and JSON mode are supported in the Responses API, Chat Completions API, Assistants API, Fine-tuning API and Batch API.

We recommend always using Structured Outputs instead of JSON mode when possible.

However, Structured Outputs with `response_format: {type: "json_schema", ...}` is only supported with the `gpt-4o-mini`, `gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18`, and `gpt-4o-2024-08-06` model snapshots and later.

 # Implementation Plan: Support Ticket Triage Assistant
 
 **Branch**: `001-support-ticket-triage` | **Date**: 2026-11-03 | **Spec**: [spec.md](./spec.md)
 
 **Input**: Approved feature specification and implementation constraints supplied for this plan.
 
 ## Summary
 
 Build a Python 3.12+ library and one-file command-line tool that turn a single customer ticket into a validated six-field triage decision. A deterministic guard handles empty, whitespace-only, and over-limit text before any model configuration or network access. Other tickets are sent unchanged as user data alongside one invariant system prompt to an injectable model client. The raw JSON reply is strictly parsed and validated; invalid output and service failures remain distinct, sanitized errors. The CLI handles strict UTF-8 file input and byte-exact output. The official `openai` package is the sole third-party runtime dependency. See [research.md](./research.md) for decisions and [contracts/interfaces.md](./contracts/interfaces.md) for public interfaces.
 
 ## Technical Context
 
 **Language/Version**: Python 3.12+
 
 **Primary Dependencies**: Official `openai` Python package only at runtime; standard library for all other runtime behavior.
 
 **Storage**: None. Input is one file for the CLI; no application persistence.
 
 **Testing**: Human-owned tests and evaluation components specified in the approved spec. `tests/`, `evals/`, and `.harness/` are not generated or modified by this plan.
 
 **Target Platform**: Python 3.12+ environments with access to the configured OpenAI service when model-assisted triage is required.
 
 **Project Type**: Python library plus command-line interface.
 
 **Performance Goals**: No latency or throughput target is specified. The OpenAI client timeout is 30 seconds; deterministic checks are local.
 
 **Constraints**: Exactly one third-party runtime dependency; fixed six-key contract; Unicode code-point length counting; no response repair; sanitized service errors; no output of specified sensitive patterns; the system prompt is identical for each ticket. No project/dependency manifest, tests, evals, or harness files are in scope. `.env` files must not be opened or read during this planning task.
 
 **Scale/Scope**: One ticket per library or CLI invocation; no history, persistence, attachments, UI, or multi-ticket processing.
 
 ## Constitution Check
 
 ### Pre-design gate
 
 | Principle / constraint | Plan decision | Status |
 |---|---|---|
 | I. Modular boundaries and secret isolation | Separate guard, prompt loading, model protocol/client, contract parsing, service orchestration, CLI, and optional `__main__` environment loading. Only `openai_client.py` reads model credentials and performs network activity. | PASS |
 | II. Untrusted input and deterministic guardrails | Treat the user message strictly as ticket data; reject invalid length/blank input before client creation or environment access. | PASS |
 | III. Validated contract and explicit failures | Validate every raw reply without normalization; distinguish `InvalidModelOutput` from fixed-message `ServiceError`. | PASS |
 | IV. Independent evaluation and acceptance | Keep the human-owned evaluation harness independent; map every AC in [acceptance-traceability.md](./contracts/acceptance-traceability.md). Do not produce or change evaluation files. | PASS |
 | V. Minimal dependencies and maintainability | Python 3.12+, official `openai` package only at runtime, otherwise standard library; use direct, small modules. | PASS |
 | Evaluation and scope controls | Do not create or alter `tests/`, `evals/`, or `.harness/`; no change to thresholds or harness behavior. | PASS |
 
 No violations or complexity exceptions are required.
 
 ### Post-design gate
 
 The proposed package and prompt tree preserves the boundaries and constraints above. Runtime secrets remain isolated to the OpenAI client; deterministic input refusals need no configuration. Evaluation traces are documentation only and point to human-owned components. The generated plan artifacts stay under `specs/001-support-ticket-triage/`. **Result: PASS; no unresolved clarifications.**
 
 ## Architecture and Key Decisions
 
 1. **Small, injectable module boundaries**: `guard.py` performs deterministic input validation; `contract.py` is pure parsing and invariant validation; `model_client.py` defines the replaceable protocol; `openai_client.py` owns environment reads and network access; `service.py` composes them; `cli.py` owns argument, file, and stream behavior. This satisfies Constitution I and V, NFR-001, FR-001–FR-002, FR-009–FR-013, and INV-001–INV-007.
 2. **Input gate precedes all external state**: The service checks exactly `text.strip() == ""` or `len(text) > 4000` without trimming the original ticket. It returns the deterministic `invalid_input` decision without creating a default client or reading environment configuration. This implements FR-002, FR-008, GR-001, and AC-001–AC-004/AC-045.
 3. **Fixed prompt and untrusted user message**: Load `prompts/system.md` relative to the package location and send it unchanged for each call; pass the exact ticket text only as the user message. The prompt requires the JSON contract and addresses categories, priority, ambiguity, refusals, prompt injection, embedded instructions, and prohibited output. This implements FR-003–FR-007, GR-002–GR-005, and AC-021/AC-036–AC-038.
 4. **Strict contract; no repair**: Decode with `json.loads`, reject duplicate keys at every object depth via `object_pairs_hook`, reject non-standard constants via `parse_constant`, and validate exact keys, types, enums, action-field consistency, lengths, refusal provenance, and prohibited patterns. Raise `InvalidModelOutput` with the exact original string on every failure. This implements FR-009, FR-011, INV-001–INV-007, and SC-001/SC-003.
 5. **Explicit OpenAI adapter and safe service errors**: Create the client inside `complete()` after verifying stripped, nonempty `OPENAI_API_KEY` and `OPENAI_MODEL`; configure 30-second timeout and no SDK retries; make one Chat Completions JSON-object request without a temperature override. Return `""` for null content. Catch only `openai.OpenAIError` and raise `ServiceError` with no cause or underlying text. This implements FR-010, NFR-001, and AC-019–AC-020/AC-050–AC-051. Evaluation retries, where applicable, belong to the separate human-owned evaluator (FR-019), not the library client.
 6. **Byte-defined CLI behavior**: Accept exactly one path, read bytes, strictly decode UTF-8 without newline translation, remove one leading U+FEFF, then call the same library function. Serialize with sorted keys, compact separators, and `ensure_ascii=False`; write UTF-8 plus one LF to the binary stream. Catch only the specified service/contract errors at the CLI boundary and map file/argument failures separately. This implements FR-012–FR-013 and AC-022–AC-029/AC-044–AC-045/AC-055.
 7. **Evaluation remains independently owned**: The specification’s dataset, scoring, retries, and run status requirements are traced to the human-owned `evals/` components. This plan neither implements nor creates evaluation or test files, consistent with Constitution IV and its scope controls. FR-014–FR-019, EV-001–EV-004, and AC-039–AC-043/AC-052–AC-054 are verification references only.
 8. **Optional `.env` convenience belongs only to the executable entry point**: `env_loader.py` may parse key/value lines when `__main__.py` starts, setting only variables not already present. Library calls do not load `.env`. No `.env` file is opened, read, printed, or modified during planning. This respects Constitution I and FR-010.

 # Quickstart and Validation Guide
 
 This guide describes how the human engineer can validate the implementation after the runtime package and human-owned test/evaluation components exist. It does not create tests, evaluation data, or harness files.
 
 ## Prerequisites
 
 - Python 3.12 or later.
 - The official `openai` package installed in the active environment for a live model call.
 - For live calls only, nonempty `OPENAI_API_KEY` and `OPENAI_MODEL` values. Do not place credentials in source control or evidence.
 - The human-owned test and evaluation components required by the approved specification.
 
 The library and CLI support an injected fake `ModelClient`, so deterministic contract and CLI checks do not require credentials or network access.
 
 ## Run the CLI
 
 From the Part-1B project root in PowerShell, configure the source package path and model settings, then pass one existing UTF-8 ticket file:
 
 ```powershell
 $env:PYTHONPATH = "src"
 $env:OPENAI_API_KEY = "<configured-key>"
 $env:OPENAI_MODEL = "<configured-model>"
 python -m ticket_triage .\ticket.txt
 ```
 
 Expected behavior: one compact JSON object followed by one LF on success. A blank ticket returns the deterministic `invalid_input` refusal without requiring either model variable. CLI errors have empty stdout and the exact stderr line/exit code in [interfaces.md](./contracts/interfaces.md).
 
 ## Validate deterministic behavior
 
 Run the human-owned unit tests with the test runner configured by the engineer. They should use an injected fake client to verify the guard boundaries (empty, whitespace-only, 4000, 4001 code points), exact user-message preservation, system-prompt stability, contract rejection, exception data, and CLI bytes/status.
 
 The acceptance-criterion-to-component mapping is in [acceptance-traceability.md](./contracts/acceptance-traceability.md). In particular, verify duplicate-key and non-finite JSON rejection, exact raw-reply preservation, 12/13-digit and API-key-pattern boundaries, BOM removal, CR/LF counting, UTF-8 non-ASCII serialization, and zero output on CLI error.
 
 ## Validate the independent evaluation
 
 The human-owned evaluation must validate its dataset and then apply Layers 1–3 as specified in the feature spec (FR-014–FR-019; EV-001–EV-004). Verify independently that Layers 1 and 2 run for returned decisions and exact raw replies in `InvalidModelOutput`, service errors are retried up to three total attempts, and an unresolved service error makes the run `INVALID`. Do not add or modify evaluator components as part of this plan.
 
 ## Reference contracts
 
 - Runtime entity shapes and invariants: [data-model.md](./data-model.md)
 - Library, model adapter, and CLI behavior: [interfaces.md](./contracts/interfaces.md)
 - Every acceptance criterion's implementation and human-owned verification location: [acceptance-traceability.md](./contracts/acceptance-traceability.md)
